plain: Poor or dishonest management of public business

webster.text: Bad management of public affairs; vicious or defective conduct in administration, or the performance of official duties, particularly of executive and ministerial duties, prescribed by law; as the maladministration of a king, or of any chief magistrate.

example.quote: An election of every four years will prevent maladministration.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, September 8, 1787
